profile.summary: GPN-Star is a DNA language model that predicts how strongly each position of a genome is constrained by evolution, and so how damaging a single-nucleotide variant there is likely to be. It reads a window of a whole-genome alignment of many species with their species tree, predicts masked nucleotides of the target genome, and scores a variant by how much less likely the alternate allele is than the reference. Human models exist at vertebrate, mammal and primate timescales, and further models cover five model organisms.

summary_quotes.text: GPN-Star uses an encoder-only architecture trained with a masked language modelling (MLM) objective. Each input consists of a WGA window and its species tree.
Trained on alignments spanning vertebrate, mammal and primate evolutionary timescales
By predicting masked nucleotides from sequence context, gLMs estimate per-site likelihoods that reflect evolutionary constraint without requiring labelled data.
The output `score` is the raw, uncalibrated alternate-minus-reference log-likelihood ratio averaged over forward and reverse-complement sequence orientations.
we train GPN-Star for five model organisms

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: GPN-Star is an encoder-only Transformer trained to predict masked nucleotides. Each input is a window of a whole-genome alignment and its species tree. The alignment is split into target sequences and source sequences. Source species that are closely related are pooled into clade-level representations. Each encoder block has self-attention along the target sequence, a phylogeny-informed cross-attention module that reads the source sequences weighted by evolutionary distances from the species tree, and a feed-forward network. The published vertebrate human checkpoint has 16 layers, hidden size 1024 and 16 attention heads.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Main, Fig. 1 legend and model description; config.json

quotes.text: The alignment is partitioned into target and source sequences and the model predicts masked nucleotides in the targets conditioned on both their sequence context and the evolutionary information in the sources.

each comprising a sequence-wise self-attention module to encode intrasequence context, a phylogeny-informed cross-attention module to encode evolutionary context from the source sequences and a feed-forward network to integrate the information.
we group closely related source species according to their evolutionary distances and pool their sequences into clade-level representations.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Eight checkpoints are published. Three are human (hg38) models of 200M parameters each, trained on a 100-way vertebrate, a 447-way mammalian and a 243-way primate alignment; the paper calls them GPN-Star (V), (M) and (P). Five are for model organisms: mouse and chicken (85M parameters), fly (85M), worm and arabidopsis (25M). Each checkpoint needs the alignment it was trained on, with matching assembly, species set, species order and evolutionary scale. Genome-wide scores are published, so many uses need no inference. A result should name the checkpoint and its Hugging Face revision, whether published scores or new inference were used, and the window size.

quotes.text: Throughout this study, we denote these models as GPN-Star (V), GPN-Star (M) and GPN-Star (P), respectively.
GPN-Star inference requires a prepared whole-genome alignment that matches the target assembly, species set, species order, and evolutionary scale used by the checkpoint.
[`songlab/gpn-star-scores`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/songlab/gpn-star-scores): genome-wide scores and UCSC Genome Browser tracks.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Phylogeny-aware masked DNA language model over whole-genome alignments

quotes.text: GPN-Star is a phylogeny-aware genomic language model trained on whole-genome alignments across multiple evolutionary timescales.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Encoder-only Transformer (GPNStarForMaskedLM) with sequence-wise self-attention and phylogeny-informed cross-attention to clade-level source embeddings. The vertebrate human checkpoint: 16 layers, hidden size 1024, 16 attention heads, intermediate size 4096.

quotes.text: GPN-Star uses an encoder-only architecture trained with a masked language modelling (MLM) objective.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A window of a prepared whole-genome alignment with its species tree, read from a local Zarr store that matches the checkpoint. Variant scoring takes biallelic single-nucleotide variants with one-based positions and an even window size.

quotes.text: Each input consists of a WGA window and its species tree.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: A raw, uncalibrated log-likelihood ratio per variant; masked-nucleotide logits; or embeddings. The paper's analyses use scores calibrated for mutation rate, which is a separate step.

quotes.text: GPN-Star VEP outputs a raw, uncalibrated LLR. Any checkpoint-specific calibration is a separate downstream operation.
Unless otherwise specified, all analyses in this study use these calibrated scores to capture functional constraints with minimal mutation rate biases.

strengths.text: Genome-wide scores are published for the human genome and the five model organisms, so variants can be looked up without running the model.
strengths.source_locator: Paper: Data availability; docs/models/gpn-star.md: Alignments and scores

quotes.text: Precomputed GPN-Star predictions for all possible single nucleotide variants in the human genome and the five model organisms are available on Hugging Face

strengths.text: Training cost is modest by the authors' account: the 200 million parameter models were trained for several days on 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs.

quotes.text: we focus here on the largest models (200 million parameters), trained for several days on 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs

strengths.text: Separate human models at three evolutionary timescales let a user choose; the authors report that deeper timescales better capture coding and highly constrained regions, and shallower ones better inform fast-evolving regulatory elements.

quotes.text: Models trained on deeper timescales better capture coding and other highly constrained regions, whereas shallower timescales better inform rapidly evolving regulatory elements

strengths.text: Code and weights are MIT licensed, and the package supports both inference and training on prepared alignments.
strengths.source_locator: README.md; Hugging Face API response; docs/models/gpn-star.md: opening paragraph

quotes.text: The maintained package supports inference and training on prepared alignments and datasets.

limitations.text: Inference needs a whole-genome alignment that matches the checkpoint. The human vertebrate archive is about 42 GB compressed, more once extracted, and the command-line tool does not download it.

quotes.text: A practical limitation is that GPN-Star requires WGAs during inference.
Its compressed `99.zarr.tar.gz` file is about 42 GB, and the extracted Zarr store requires additional space.
The CLI deliberately does not download these large stores.

limitations.text: Variant scoring covers biallelic single-nucleotide variants. The authors say the fixed alignment format makes the model less suited to indels and structural variants.

quotes.text: VEP inputs must be biallelic SNVs
Also, the reliance on a fixed alignment format makes the model less suitable for analysing indels and structural variants.

limitations.text: Scores from the command-line tool are raw and uncalibrated. The paper's results use mutation-rate calibrated scores, so raw output is not directly comparable to them.

quotes.text: GPN-Star VEP outputs a raw, uncalibrated LLR.
Unless otherwise specified, all analyses in this study use these calibrated scores

limitations.text: The model is trained on DNA sequence alone and is not specific to any tissue.

quotes.text: GPN-Star trained solely on DNA sequences is intrinsically tissue agnostic.

run_guide.summary: Install the gpn package, load the vertebrate human checkpoint, download and arrange its alignment, and score variants from the command line.
prerequisites: For many uses no run is needed: genome-wide scores are published at https://huggingface.co/datasets/songlab/gpn-star-scores.
Python with pip. The repository badge names Python 3.13.
Disk space for the vertebrate alignment archive: about 42 GB compressed, plus more for the extracted Zarr store. The hf, sha256sum and unpigz commands are used to fetch and unpack it.

Variants as biallelic single-nucleotide variants with one-based positions. The GPN-Star section of the command-line guide does not list accepted file formats; the GPN-MSA section lists Parquet, CSV/TSV, VCF, GTF and GFF.
GPU need is not stated; inference defaults to FP32 on any device.

steps.title: Install the package with inference dependencies
steps.explanation: The inference extra is required for the file-backed commands.

steps.title: Load the checkpoint in Python
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from gpn import register_auto_classes
from transformers import AutoModelForMaskedLM

register_auto_classes("star")
model = AutoModelForMaskedLM.from_pretrained("songlab/gpn-star-hg38-v100-200m")
PY
steps.explanation: The documentation's quick start, wrapped in a shell heredoc. It downloads the weights from Hugging Face.

steps.title: Download and verify the vertebrate alignment
steps.shell:
hf download songlab/multiz100way-pigz 99.zarr.tar.gz \
  --repo-type dataset \
  --revision 6a9d42a35e7debbba845979dea6064f14d5cb3f9 \
  --local-dir .

echo '4dad7da04db9c804032c0c4c7bbefea58f694fc911e962d28c8df87f356ce4ad  99.zarr.tar.gz' \
  | sha256sum --check
unpigz --stdout 99.zarr.tar.gz | tar -xf -
steps.explanation: Copied from the documentation. The archive extracts as 99.zarr.

steps.title: Arrange the alignment store
steps.explanation: These two lines are written by Rewire from the documentation's prose, which asks for the extracted store to be moved or symlinked to /path/to/multiz100way/100/all.zarr; the directory name 100 is significant. Replace /path/to with a real location.

quotes.text: Move or symlink the extracted store to `/path/to/multiz100way/100/all.zarr`, then pass `--msa-path /path/to/multiz100way`.

steps.title: Score variants
steps.shell:
gpn star vep \
  --input-path INPUT_PATH \
  --msa-path /path/to/multiz100way \
  --window-size WINDOW_SIZE \
  --model-path songlab/gpn-star-hg38-v100-200m \
  --output-path OUTPUT_PATH
steps.explanation: The command template from the command-line guide, with the alignment path and the model name from the documentation filled in by Rewire. Replace INPUT_PATH with a variant file, WINDOW_SIZE with an even number and OUTPUT_PATH with a Parquet file name. The sources read do not give the window size for this checkpoint. Chromosome names must match the store, and the reference allele must match the alignment or inference stops.
steps.source_locator: cli.md: GPN-Star; docs/models/gpn-star.md: Inspect a local interval

quotes.text: gpn star vep \ --input-path INPUT_PATH \ --msa-path LOCAL_MSA_PATH \ --window-size WINDOW_SIZE \ --model-path MODEL_PATH \ --output-path OUTPUT_PATH
Chromosome names must match the store.

outputs: A Parquet file at OUTPUT_PATH with one row per input variant and a score column: the raw, uncalibrated alternate-minus-reference log-likelihood ratio. Negative values mean the alternate allele is less likely than the reference.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The window size for the published checkpoints is not given in the sources read, and scores depend on it.
Other checkpoints need their own matching alignment; only the vertebrate human alignment has download steps in the documentation read.

notes: Both existing sources (vep-uc-20261014-source-gpn-star and gpn-star-20261116-source-nature-2026) are the same Nature paper read here as @paper via Europe PMC (CC BY 4.0, so store_bytes is true). The source ID prefix gpn-star-20261116 suggests a second GPN-Star model record may exist in the store; check for a duplicate before applying.
